messages:
anika: quick postmortem-style note from yesterday's canary: we saw elevated eviction churn tied to small epoch bumps during tenant rebalances. wanted to capture ideas before we forget. :coffee:

anika: symptom: when shard_epoch changes frequently, local cache items get stamped invalid and we trigger a storm of revalidation reads + evictions. p99 CPU on inference nodes spiked ~18%.

brad: ouch. did we correlate to tenant size/hotkey concentration?

anika: yes — small tenants with heavy hotkeys (single prefix) caused the worst ripples. coalescing didn't kick in because revalidations were per-key, not per-prefix.

samir: initial theory: stamping each cache entry with epoch makes invalidation simple but noisy. maybe we can move to a two-tier approach: prefix-level epoch + per-entry generation. then invalidation can fast-reject at prefix boundary and coalesce revalidations for that prefix.

tess: sketch: store prefix_meta.epoch and entry.generation. On epoch bump, mark prefix_meta.quarantine_until = now + jitter_window. Readers hitting quarantined prefix do one of: 1) coalesced sync revalidate if no in-flight revalidation; 2) serve stale with header for best-effort paths. Coalescer holds a single in-flight revalidation per prefix.

anika: that sounds promising. main goals: avoid N concurrent revalidations for M keys under the same prefix change, and avoid mass evictions that thrash GC.

samir: added idea: make quarantine adaptive by estimating prefix hotness: if hotness > threshold, extend quarantine to allow coalescing; if not, shorten and let reads fetch from store. Hotness calc = moving avg of hits/sec.

brad: we should be careful with memory accounting. If we keep items while quarantined we need a soft-pin that prevents immediate eviction but still counts toward pressure metrics. we can't leak memory. propose soft_pin_ttl = min(5s, 10% of prefix_hot_window).

tess: also consider a background revalidate sweep that samples keys from the prefix rather than immediate full-populate. that reduces immediate load on store. tradeoff: some reads may still see stale data until their key is touched. acceptable for eventual-read paths.

anika: interplay with ownership handoffs: we need to ensure new owner adopts prefix_meta atomically. else we get double-quarantine or missed quaratine. ownership adopt should transfer prefix_meta with epoch and any active coalescer ownership token.

samir: proposal for coalescer ownership token: when owner B takes over, it can attempt to acquire coalescer token for prefix. if owner A had in-flight coalescer, handoff RPC transfers in-flight state or marks it as orphaned and owner B retries with exponential backoff.

brad: handoff RPC complexity worries me. maybe easier: mandate short grace window where owner A continues serving reads for quarantined prefixes while owner B warms. That reduces handoff complexity but increases cross-owner serving duration.

tess: we can combine: cheap handoff where owner B probes owner A for coalescer leader for specific prefix via metadata endpoint; if owner A responds with leader info, owner B waits or coordinates. If no response in 100ms, owner B starts new coalescer. simple best-effort handoff.

anika: ok. for correctness we should formalize invariants: (1) any linearized read after a committed write must observe the write; (2) no more than one active revalidation for a prefix at a time per shard (best-effort); (3) memory usage must not exceed configured soft-reserve budget during quarantine.

samir: tests: unit tests for coalescer state machine, integration fuzz that bumps epochs while hitting hot prefixes, and a load test measuring revalidation amplification (want <1.2x extra store-reads for hot prefixes).

brad: metrics to add: prefix_quarantine_count, prefix_coalescer_inflight, prefix_coalescer_revalidate_latency_ms, prefix_hotness_rate, prefix_softpin_memory_bytes. Also emit event when handoff probe fails.

tess: rollout plan: behind feature flag. Stage 1 = read-only telemetry + canary with soft_pin disabled. Stage 2 = enable soft_pin for hot prefixes only. Stage 3 = enable full coalescer. Each stage runs 48h and we watch p99 CPU, revalidation rate, and store ops uplift.

anika: one subtlety: eviction scoring currently uses recency + weight. quarantined items should get boosted score to keep them around. but that biases eviction fairness. So only boost within soft-reserve pool and continue normal scoring for the rest.

samir: agree. implementation note: add eviction_bucket: SOFT_QUARANTINE. items there are protected until soft_pin_ttl expires or prefix exits quarantine. evict from SOFT_QUARANTINE only after other buckets drained.

brad: perf micro-optimizations: prefix_meta should be a compact struct in the shard's read path so epoch compare is a single load. coalescer uses lock-free single-writer queue for waiting waiters. keep cost < 10ns on happy path.

tess: I'll prototype the prefix_meta layout and coalescer API. plan to open a draft PR with bench results.

anika: thanks. action items: tess -> prototype + PR; samir -> design doc with state machine and tests; brad -> eviction budget + memory semantics; anika -> write canary scenarios and run initial telemetry.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: k8s-canary-3 -> 2026-03-23T04:30Z; will post results to #eng-runtime.

anika: thanks all. if we see >3% store read amplification or >10% extra p99 latency we revert the flag.

anika: end of thread.
